problem: "Both lines fall in the direction of flow when there is no pump" is stated as an absolute rule, but the very next paragraph says the HGL can rise in a diffuser. A student reading the first line will mark the second statement as wrong.
fix: "The TEL always falls in the direction of flow when there is no pump. The HGL usually falls with it, but it can rise where the velocity head drops faster than the TEL (a diffuser)."

problem: "It must be at least one velocity head above the HGL" is loose. The gap is exactly V²/(2g) at a section, not a minimum.
fix: "The TEL is exactly one velocity head above the HGL at every section; the two lines meet only where V = 0, such as a reservoir surface."

problem: "Every friction length" is unclear; a student may read it as a special term.
fix: "Every metre of pipe friction and every fitting pulls the TEL down."
